title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement: You get a string of capital letters and a number k. You may change at most k letters to any other letter. After the changes, find the length of the longest stretch made of one repeated letter.

example.caption: With k = 2, swap the two A letters in ABAB for B. The whole string becomes BBBB, length 4.

idea.sentence: A window can be fixed if its size minus its most common letter count is at most k. Slide the window and never let it shrink.

jargon.plain: The stretch of the string between a left and a right marker.
The highest count one letter has reached inside any window so far.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the string, then k, e.g. "AABABBA", 1

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Count letters in every substring and test the rule.

rows.name: Sliding window
rows.note: Each step adds one letter and removes at most one. The count table holds at most 26 capital letters.

fast.takeaway: Only the window size matters for the answer. A window that cannot grow just slides along, so you never need to recompute the top count.

stages.title: Counts and maxFreq
stages.note: A table of letter counts for the window, and the highest count seen so far.

stages.title: Grow on the right
stages.note: Count the new letter and raise maxFreq if this letter has a new top count.

stages.title: Too many replacements: slide
stages.note: If size minus maxFreq is more than k, drop the left letter. The window keeps its size.

stages.title: Size is the answer
stages.note: The window only grows when it finds a better one, so its final size is the best length.

edges.title: No replacements
edges.why: With k = 0 the window can only hold one letter type at a time. The longest run is length 1.

edges.title: k is huge
edges.why: You can turn everything into one letter, so the whole string counts. The window never slides.

edges.title: Stale maxFreq
edges.why: After the best window passes, maxFreq stays at its high mark. The window only grows if a letter beats that mark, which is exactly when a longer answer exists.

edges.title: Single letter
edges.why: One letter is already a run of length 1.

gotchas.text: Do not lower maxFreq when the left letter leaves. It looks wrong, but a stale high value can only make the window slide, never grow, so the answer stays correct.
The window is not always valid after a slide. Only its size matters. Return the final size, which is the length minus left.
Map.get returns undefined for a missing key. Default with ?? 0 before adding or subtracting, or the count becomes NaN.
count[s[right]]++ works on a missing key because the zero value of int is 0. Keys are bytes, so print them with string(rune(b)).

recap.pattern: Sliding window: size minus top count
recap.key: A window needs (size minus its most common letter count) replacements. If that exceeds k, slide it right. Never shrink it.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(1) for 26 letters.
moves: Count each letter that enters the window
Raise maxFreq if this letter's count is a new high
If size minus maxFreq is more than k, drop the left letter and move left
Return length minus left, which is the final window size
